upstreamFacts.countDiscrepancy: The upstream root README reports 286 skills while .codex-plugin/README.md reports 281. Factory treats counts as informational only and pins decisions to the audited commit.

components.reason: Use individual workflows only after overlap, security, context-cost and behavioral evaluation. Never bulk-import the catalog.
Use routing patterns as references while preserving one Factory router and bounded agent activation.
Adopt project-scoped observations, atomic reusable patterns and confidence as signals; replace direct evolution/auto-promotion with Factory evidence, regression and policy gates.
Keep active context small; persist durable project state and archive raw sessions/logs outside the reasoning window.
Plan/test/implement/review/verify is useful when producer, reviewer and verifier have genuinely separated evidence/context rather than theatrical role multiplication.
Its agent-infrastructure scan surfaces match Factory needs, but the scanner package/action remains executable third-party code and requires its own pinned security audit before CI enforcement.
Deterministic observation hooks are valuable; arbitrary upstream hooks must never be enabled during initial intake.
Only relevant language/project rule packs may be normalized; no broad always-loaded context.
Role prompts may inform specialist design, but agent count is not capability and bulk agent import is prohibited.
Useful command entry points should become capability/skill routing rather than a second command architecture.
Normalize external connectors behind canonical Factory tools; no MCP server gains authority from installation alone.
Do not install the full ECC plugin into the active Factory Codex environment until duplication, hook, MCP, context and routing conflicts are tested.

factoryAdaptations.skillAcquisition: RUN -> OBSERVE -> CANDIDATE_SKILL -> EVIDENCE_CHECK -> REGRESSION_TEST -> POLICY_OR_HUMAN_GATE -> PROMOTE -> SKILL_REGISTRY
factoryAdaptations.verification: PRODUCE -> VALIDATE -> PASS:SHIP | FAIL:REPAIR -> REVALIDATE -> bounded attempts/escalation

risks: Bulk importing hundreds of skills would inflate routing and context cost.
Hooks are executable authority surfaces and require independent review before trust.
Codex plugin installation may register MCP/hook surfaces and must not be combined with legacy sync.
ECC continuous learning can evolve/promote patterns more aggressively than Factory policy allows.
AgentShield itself is third-party executable code and cannot bootstrap its own trust decision.
Upstream counts and adapter support are volatile and must be snapshot-pinned.
promotionRules: No ECC component becomes Factory-wide merely because it exists upstream.
Pattern-only extraction may proceed from static audited source.
Executable adoption requires pinned source, security review, sandbox and regression evidence.
Project-local success is not global proof.
Cross-project promotion requires independent repeated success plus Factory self-improvement gates.
Never enable upstream hooks, MCP servers, installers or background observers during first-pass repository intake.
